article.title: Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns
article.description: Countable nouns have a singular/plural form and can follow numbers: 'one apple, two apples.' Uncountable nouns have no plural and can't follow numbers directly: 'information' (not 'informations'), 'advice', 'furniture', 'water'. Use 'much' with uncountable nouns and 'many' with countable: 'How much water?' vs 'How many apples?'
article.content: Countable nouns have a singular/plural form and can follow numbers: 'one apple, two apples.' Uncountable nouns have no plural and can't follow numbers directly: 'information' (not 'informations'), 'advice', 'furniture', 'water'. Use 'much' with uncountable nouns and 'many' with countable: 'How much water?' vs 'How many apples?'

generated.caption:
Ever paused before asking "how much" or "how many"? 🤔

Here's the quick difference! Countable nouns have singular/plural forms (like 'one apple, two apples'). Uncountable nouns don't (like 'information' or 'water'). Use "many" for countable things, and "much" for uncountable things.

For example: "How many apples?" vs. "How much water?" Easy! 😉

Inki singular aur plural form hoti hai. Lekin uncountable nouns ko count nahi kar sakte. Inki koi plural form nahi hoti, jaise 'information', 'advice', 'furniture', 'water'. slides.body: Countable nouns refer to things we can count individually and have both singular and plural forms, such as 'one apple' or 'two apples.' Uncountable nouns, on the other hand, cannot be counted individually and do not have a plural form; examples include 'information' (not 'informations'), 'advice', 'furniture', or 'water.' To express quantity, remember to use 'many' with countable nouns ('How many apples?') and 'much' with uncountable nouns ('How much water?').
